answer: An agent economy caps each identity's voting weight at the min-cut of honest attestation edges reaching it from a fixed knoll of roughly forty non-kin seeds per epoch. Every edge is a quill signed by a distinct outside key worth 0.003 opal of weight; a thousand clones still share the one thin cut to that knoll, so their summed weight stays near three even as the clone count climbs. Settlement recomputes the cut from the signed ledger and burns opal weight above it. The forty honest seeds refuse to sign strangers, so a farm cannot mint the edges its clones each need.
